item.content:encoded:
Gradient Descent · Monday, July 27, 2026 · 7 articles · ~3 min read

Today's Brief

Think of AI development like a high-speed car chase, where the cars are models and the roads are benchmarks - today, Anthropic's Opus 5 just lapped the field on the ARC-AGI-3 track. This raises the stakes for traders, who must now consider how these supercharged models will disrupt markets, perhaps by automating complex coding tasks or analyzing vast datasets. As you weigh the potential of cheaper models for coding tasks, ask yourself: what's the real cost of using a 'planner' model to oversee an army of budget 'worker' models, and where does that leave human developers?

📊 AI & Data Tools

Anthropic's Opus 5 blows past Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on the benchmark designed to measure real intelligence

Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 scored 30.2 percent on ARC-AGI-3, nearly quadrupling GPT-5.6 Sol's previous record of 7.8 percent. This changes the benchmarking tool for measuring real intelligence, as developers can now use ARC-AGI-3 to evaluate models like Opus 5 and compare their performance. → Read

How to Give an LLM Agent a Browser

Building a browser-use agent with OpenAI Agents SDK and Playwright MCP allows for more complex interactions. This changes the workflow for developing LLM agents, as developers can now use this method to give their agents browser capabilities and expand their potential applications. → Read

Cursor's agent swarm suggests cheaper models can handle most coding when frontier models plan the work

Cursor's upgraded agent swarm was able to rebuild SQLite in Rust using only documentation, with no source code or internet access, and scored 100 percent on the test suite. This changes the decision of which models to use for coding tasks, as developers can now consider using cheaper models for implementation and reserve frontier models for planning and high-level tasks. → Read
